caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular wooden sign framed with a natural wood color frame, hanging horizontally from a dark rod at the top. The central image shows a plate of food, rendered in shades of orange and brown, resembling fried or baked pieces possibly meat, placed on a blue and white plate. Behind the plate, there is a water pitcher or jug, painted in blue and white tones, partially obscured by the plate. Below the plate, there are two crossed utensils—a fork on the right and a knife on the left—each with metallic silver blades and brown handles. The background of the upper section of the sign appears to be a weathered wood texture in light tan with visible grain patterns. The bottom section of the sign contains dark lettering, partially obscured, in white or light gray paint, reading “WYL. GORDON” against a black or dark gray background. The entire composition is vertically split in the middle where the wooden sign consists of two planks joined together.
title: William Gordon's Tavern Sign
